title: Product Design
description: A practice-heavy, evidence-first pathway from complete beginner to junior product-design capability across research, UX, UI, interaction, responsive systems, accessibility, prototyping, testing, handoff, and portfolio presentation.

target.role: Junior Product Designer, UI/UX Designer, Junior UX Designer, or Junior UI Designer
target.learner: A complete beginner with basic computer literacy and no assumed design, research, Figma, HTML/CSS, accessibility, product-team, or professional communication experience.
target.professionalOutcome: Take a reasonably scoped digital-product problem from research and problem definition through interaction and visual design, responsive prototyping, usability testing, iteration, accessibility review, developer handoff, and professional case-study presentation under normal junior supervision.
specialGoals: Build genuine Figma dexterity through product work while keeping all required outcomes possible on the free Starter route.
Produce portfolio-ready artifacts and case studies without fabricated users, personas, metrics, or outcomes.
Develop compatible collaboration and handoff habits for work with front-end and back-end engineering graduates.

phases.title: Design Foundations
phases.outcome: Establish an evidence-first product-design practice, organized Figma workspace, critique habits, and the ability to interpret a bounded brief.

phases.title: Research and Problem Definition
phases.outcome: Plan and conduct ethical beginner-scale research, separate observations from assumptions, synthesize evidence, and frame useful product problems.

phases.title: Information and Interaction
phases.outcome: Structure content around user mental models, create flows and wireframes, and design complete interaction states rather than isolated screens.

phases.title: Visual and Responsive Systems
phases.outcome: Apply typography, color, spacing, responsive layout, components, and system thinking to coherent multi-device interfaces.

phases.title: Testing, Accessibility, and Handoff
phases.outcome: Prototype, test, iterate, review accessibility, and communicate implementation-ready decisions with product and engineering partners.

phases.title: Professional Product Practice
phases.outcome: Connect design to goals and metrics, manage scoped work, complete an independent capstone, and present credible portfolio evidence.

competencies.name: Evidence-first product design
competencies.description: Frame product design as an iterative practice that connects user evidence, product goals, constraints, designed behavior, and measured learning.

competencies.name: Figma workspace and file hygiene
competencies.description: Create, name, organize, share, and export Figma files using frames, layers, pages, and version-conscious professional habits.

competencies.name: Critique and design rationale
competencies.description: Give and receive specific critique, distinguish preference from evidence, and explain a design decision with observable reasoning.

competencies.name: Briefs, requirements, and scope
competencies.description: Interpret a product brief, identify ambiguity, ask useful questions, state assumptions, and define a feasible design scope.

competencies.name: Research questions and method choice
competencies.description: Turn product uncertainty into research questions and select a proportionate qualitative or quantitative method.

competencies.name: Research ethics, consent, and privacy
competencies.description: Recruit and work with participants ethically, obtain informed consent, minimize collected data, and document limitations.

competencies.name: Interviews and contextual observation
competencies.description: Plan and conduct neutral interviews or observation, take evidence-based notes, and avoid leading participants.

competencies.name: Surveys, sampling, and bias
competencies.description: Use surveys only when appropriate, write neutral questions, recognize sampling limits, and avoid overstating results.

competencies.name: Research synthesis and insights
competencies.description: Separate observations, patterns, findings, insights, and recommendations through traceable collaborative synthesis.

competencies.name: Problem framing and outcomes
competencies.description: Write evidence-backed problem statements, define outcome-oriented opportunities, and keep solutions separate from needs.

competencies.name: Journeys and task flows
competencies.description: Map an evidence-backed current journey and create task flows that expose decisions, branches, failure points, and recovery.

competencies.name: Information architecture and labeling
competencies.description: Organize content, name categories in user language, define navigation hierarchy, and explain the underlying mental model.

competencies.name: Card sorting and tree testing
competencies.description: Choose and run a bounded card sort or tree test, interpret limitations, and revise information architecture from evidence.

competencies.name: Sketching and concept divergence
competencies.description: Generate multiple low-cost concepts before convergence and compare them against evidence, constraints, and task outcomes.

competencies.name: Wireframing
competencies.description: Create low-fidelity wireframes that communicate hierarchy, content, navigation, and task behavior without premature polish.

competencies.name: Usability heuristics and evaluation
competencies.description: Apply established usability heuristics to identify, prioritize, and communicate interface risks without substituting inspection for user testing.

competencies.name: Interaction patterns and feedback
competencies.description: Design discoverable controls, navigation, feedback, confirmations, progressive disclosure, and reversible actions.

competencies.name: Forms and system states
competencies.description: Design forms, validation, errors, empty states, loading states, success states, permissions, and destructive actions as coherent flows.

competencies.name: Visual hierarchy and composition
competencies.description: Use scale, contrast, grouping, alignment, whitespace, density, and rhythm to communicate priority and relationships.

competencies.name: Typography systems
competencies.description: Choose readable type, establish a purposeful scale, control line length and spacing, and preserve hierarchy across viewports.

competencies.name: Color, contrast, and color independence
competencies.description: Build restrained semantic palettes, verify contrast, avoid color-only meaning, and document accessible color decisions.

competencies.name: Grids, spacing, imagery, and iconography
competencies.description: Apply coherent grids and spacing scales and select licensed imagery and recognizable icons that support content.

competencies.name: Responsive and multi-device design
competencies.description: Prioritize content and adapt layout, navigation, controls, and touch targets across narrow, medium, and wide contexts.

competencies.name: Figma auto layout and constraints
competencies.description: Build adaptable Figma frames with auto layout, resizing, constraints, and content stress tests.

competencies.name: Components, variants, and states
competencies.description: Create reusable components and variants whose names, properties, states, and overrides remain understandable.

competencies.name: Design-system foundations and tokens
competencies.description: Define a small system of foundations, semantic tokens, components, patterns, and usage guidance without premature over-systematization.

competencies.name: Interactive prototyping
competencies.description: Choose an appropriate fidelity and create task-focused prototype flows with meaningful feedback and realistic content.

competencies.name: Usability-test planning and moderation
competencies.description: Write neutral task scenarios, recruit representative participants, moderate without teaching, and capture observable behavior.

competencies.name: Findings, prioritization, and iteration
competencies.description: Convert test observations into traceable findings, prioritize by evidence and risk, and iterate without chasing every opinion.

competencies.name: WCAG-aware interface review
competencies.description: Apply relevant WCAG 2.2 principles to contrast, reflow, target size, focus, labels, errors, content, and non-text information.

competencies.name: Inclusive interaction and assistive-technology awareness
competencies.description: Anticipate keyboard, screen-reader, zoom, reduced-motion, cognitive, motor, hearing, and situational needs in design and testing.

competencies.name: Frontend implementation literacy
competencies.description: Explain how semantic HTML, CSS layout, breakpoints, components, content, and browser behavior constrain and enable a design.

competencies.name: Developer handoff and design QA
competencies.description: Prepare inspectable specifications, assets, states, responsive rules, acceptance notes, and constructive implementation QA.

competencies.name: Product goals, metrics, and tradeoffs
competencies.description: Connect design choices to user value, business constraints, feasibility, qualitative evidence, and bounded success measures.

competencies.name: Team workflow, tickets, and estimation
competencies.description: Work from tickets and briefs, decompose design work, estimate uncertainty, communicate progress, and collaborate asynchronously.

competencies.name: Stakeholder, client, and freelance communication
competencies.description: Set scope and revision boundaries, present uncertainty, negotiate feedback, document decisions, and hand over work professionally.

competencies.name: Responsible AI-assisted design
competencies.description: Use AI for bounded ideation, organization, critique, and repetitive work while protecting privacy and rejecting fabricated research or evidence.

competencies.name: Asset licensing and attribution
competencies.description: Select fonts, icons, images, and templates with appropriate licenses, attribution, privacy, and reuse discipline.

competencies.name: Portfolio case-study construction
competencies.description: Build concise case studies that connect problem, evidence, decisions, iterations, outcome, limitations, and learning without invented metrics.

competencies.name: Professional presentation and storytelling
competencies.description: Present a scoped design narrative, adapt detail to the audience, answer challenges honestly, and make evidence inspectable.

competencies.name: Independent end-to-end product design
competencies.description: Independently plan, execute, test, document, and present a reasonably scoped digital-product design under normal junior supervision.

graduation.outcome: Independently investigate, design, prototype, test, iterate, accessibility-review, hand off, and present a reasonably scoped digital-product experience with honest evidence and professional judgment.

assumptions: The required route uses only free resources and Figma Starter capabilities; paid Dev Mode, paid libraries, advanced prototyping, and AI add-ons are optional and never assessed prerequisites.
A modern browser, email address for the selected design tool, and the ability to create and share files are available.
Real participants are preferred when ethical and feasible; secondary or simulated work must be labeled, and fabricated research evidence is prohibited.
Proof records learner-submitted evidence and remains distinct from independent verification under the existing XcelerateAI evidence model.
Tool-specific instruction serves transferable product-design capability; visual imitation or software-button recall alone does not satisfy graduation.
